players.name: António João Pereira de Albuquerque Tavares da Silva

1.headline: Haaland captains everywhere, returns nowhere — Woolly strolls, Rob wins a one-point thriller
1.introduction: Gameweek 1 served the full Super 8s starter pack: a proper last-minute gasp (Rob v Paul), a 21-point hammering (Woolly), and about half the league putting the armband on Haaland only to be rewarded with a communal shrug. João Pedro quietly did the job for loads of teams while plenty of managers clocked up wasted bench points they’ll pretend were tactical.

matches.title: Richard 56 — 57 Prince Majid Rd FC (Rich v Rami)
matches.text: A one-point skirmish to open the week and Rami got the win despite a modest 57. Rich had Bruno as captain and got a doubled 4 — brave, if slightly baffling — while Rami’s João Pedro again chipped in with 11, the little engine that is annoyingly reliable. Rich will tell anyone who listens that it was close; Rami will tell you he always meant to do that (and possibly that living abroad is good for concentration).

matches.title: Humorous Name United 72 — 71 Roped in again (Rob v Paul)
matches.text: The highest-scoring tie of the week and the one to give you palpitations: 143 points combined and Rob won by a single point. Both sides had João Pedro on 11; Rob’s Bruno captaincy paid 4 and Paul’s Haaland captain did the same — so the deciding differences were everywhere else. Paul can console himself by saying he scored 71 and still lost, which is a reliably painful Super 8s experience.

matches.title: Change Name FC 67 — 76 Bielsa's Babes (Dave v Paddy)
matches.text: Patrick top-scored for the week with 76 — the highest individual team tally — and managed it despite giving the armband to Haaland (4). His midfield double-figures — including Benjamin White and João Pedro — did the heavy lifting. David’s 67 was plenty respectable; awkward for him that it still reads as 'conceded 76' in the record books.

matches.title: el Guapo 47 — 51 BeLucky Again (Tom v Kev)
matches.text: Lowest-scoring match of the GW and not exactly a classic. Tom scraped 47 and Kev got 51, which is a comfortable enough margin to go off and hit the golf course for a celebratory nine holes. Several managers will blame captaincy choices; Kev will blame nothing and quietly enjoy his 3 points.

matches.title: FC Dangerous 50 — 50 Seattle Scorchers (Watson v Crystal)
matches.text: The narrowest result — actually not a result at all — a 50-50 draw. Both managers picked similar-looking squads and both came away with the same total, which is either poetic symmetry or utter lack of imagination. Martin Ødegaard and João Pedro turned up for both sides, while both captains (Haaland on both benches?) delivered modest returns.

matches.title: ChampagneSuperRovers 55 — 59 Atletico Waspo (Dunne v Foz)
matches.text: Foz’s Atletico edged James’ ChampagneSuperRovers by four. João Pedro again popped up with 11 for the winners, and Ben’s defence of players with quiet scores did the job. James will point to a few missed opportunities; Ben will point to his bank balance (metaphorically) and the scoreboard.

matches.title: Woolbrohampton 71 — 50 Turf Less (Woolly v Bradshaw)
matches.text: Biggest winning margin of the week — Woolly’s 21-point romp. Ben put together a tidy 71 and Martyn’s Turf Less managed 50 despite Cole Palmer bringing 13 on the scoresheet for Turf Less. Woolly will enjoy the moment; Martyn will enjoy the rest of the season and possibly the occasional Burnley-related misery.

awards.text: Won 72–71. You don’t get many one‑point victories that actually feel like one point — this did. Rob edged Paul in the highest‑scoring match of the week (143 combined) and gets to bask in the glory while the rest of us clutch our chests.

Plenty of you put the armband on Haaland and watched 4 points materialise. Paul’s captain returned 4 and he lost by one. It’s the kind of cruel arithmetic only FPL can produce — impressively tragic timing.

awards.award: The Bench Bonus (But Not For You) Award
awards.text: Kevin had Anton Stach on his bench for 13 points that didn’t count plus a few more wasted bench points. You could argue it was a tactical saving for later — or that Kev was busy golfing and left his best option sitting.
Biggest margin, biggest smile. Ben’s 71‑50 win over Turf Less was the week’s most decisive result. Good start if you’re Woolly; annoying start if you’re anyone else.

1.table_commentary: The official Super 8s table — using H2H points and the FPL tie‑breaker of total points — puts Patrick’s Bielsa’s Babes top after that 76, with Rob’s Humorous Name United second on 72 and Woolbrohampton third on 71. Foz’s Atletico and Rami’s Prince Majid Rd FC follow in the top six, while Kev’s BeLucky Again sneaks into sixth as well. The mid‑table has the two 50‑point stalemates (Watson and Crystal) sharing a single point apiece. Down the other end, Martyn’s Turf Less ends the week bottom after that 21‑point defeat — not the start Burnley fans would recommend reliving.

preview.fixture: Prince Majid Rd FC v Woolbrohampton (Rami v Woolly)
preview.text: Rami travels to meet Woolly after both posted wins. Ben’s 71 suggests he’s hot out the traps; Rami’s handy 57 was good enough to edge Rich. If Rami’s João Pedro turns up again this one could be interesting — and if Woolly keeps his form it’ll be a proper test. Money versus… also money, but in different flavours.

preview.fixture: Bielsa's Babes v Humorous Name United (Paddy v Rob)
preview.text: Two of the weekend’s highest scorers meet next. Patrick had 76 and Rob 72 — both leaned on João Pedro and had mixed captain fortunes. Expect more points, a bit of mind‑reading over captaincy and a fixture that could decide who’s actually going to make life difficult at the top early on.

preview.fixture: Turf Less v ChampagneSuperRovers (Bradshaw v Dunne)
preview.text: Martyn needs a response after that 21‑point defeat and James will fancy his chances after a respectable 55. Turf Less have Cole Palmer on the books (13 this week) so if Martyn can get him firing again he might stop the rot. Otherwise it’s an awkward mid‑season chat with Burnley in the background.

1.closing: That’s it for GW1: plenty of points, questionable captaincies and a reminder that in the Super 8s you can score big and still be miserable. See you next week — and anyone putting the armband on Haaland again, perhaps try something radical like a coin flip.
